messages:
Priya N: Heads-up — MedTech's security team mailed a follow-up for the vendor SQ. They want three pieces: (1) role-to-KMS principal mapping, (2) 48h audit log sample showing decrypt/unwrap events for tenant-123, (3) proof of ephemeral credential TTL and how assume-role is restricted. Can we produce redacted artifacts?

Sam L: I can pull role mappings and logs. Quick question — do they want SIEM-friendly JSON (full event objects) or a human-readable CSV summary?

Jessica C: SIEM JSON preferred. Include event_ids and request_ids. Also call out the default STS token TTL (1h) and any exceptions we allow for internal tooling.

Mike R: For KMS evidence: we should provide envelope metadata (key_id, algorithm, key_state), a signed manifest of key creation time, and a sample wrap/unwrap audit entry. If they're BYO-KMS we will only be able to show the envelope metadata we store.

Priya N: Important: MedTech explicitly asked for a statement that only the service account(s) used by our control plane can request decrypt. So we need a clear mapping: service account -> IAM bindings -> KMS principal ID. @Sam can you export a 48h slice for tenant-123 but redact usernames and ciphertext?

Sam L: Running a query now:
```
-- audit export (redaction flags applied)
SELECT event_id, timestamp, resource, action, principal_id, request_id, status
FROM audit_logs
WHERE resource = 'encryption/decrypt' AND tenant_id = 'tenant-123' AND timestamp >= now() - interval '48 hours';
```
I'll run with principal_id pseudonymization and strip ciphertext fields.

DevBot: Export job queued (job_id=3421). Estimated completion ~6 minutes. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Security Oncall: Heads-up on export hygiene: do not include plaintext keys or unredacted principal emails. For KMS proof we can include a hashed-ciphertext value (sha256) and the request_id/status so they can correlate without seeing secrets. Also avoid any PII in metadata.

Priya N: Agreed. Also let's prepare a short narrative for the SQ: bullet list that explains our RBAC model (roles: control-plane-service, tenant-ops, auditor-readonly), how role elevation is handled (no direct human elevation; JIT tokens via bastion), and where audit logs are immutable (write-once S3 bucket path + retention policy).

Jessica C: I'll draft the narrative. For the auditor evidence, include these items:
- role mapping CSV (redacted)
- 48h audit JSON sample (redacted)
- KMS envelope metadata extract (redacted key IDs, creation_ts)
- statement of token TTL and how session tags restrict scope

Mike R: One technical nit: if we include CloudHSM logs, call out the log canonicalization step we run (we normalize timezones to UTC and include microsecond precision). Also include the KMS key rotation history entry for the tenant key (creation and last-rotate timestamps).

Sam L: Export complete. Uploaded redacted artifacts to internal share: https://files.internal/redwood/medtech-evidence/5732109999-redacted.zip

Priya N: Thanks. I'll review and assemble the SQ response. @Security Oncall, please confirm we didn't leak any PII in that package and sign off; we need to send to MedTech by EOD.

Security Oncall: Quick pass done — no PII, no plaintext keys. A few entries had full email strings; those are replaced with <redacted-email-#>. Check the CSV header for leftover internal-only columns; otherwise good to go. :white_check_mark:

Priya N: Perfect. Jessica, once you finish the narrative I will upload to the vendor portal and mark the ticket resolved.

Jessica C: Draft in progress, will ping when ready.

Mike R: One follow-up for the record — we should add a short appendix describing how we would handle an incident where a KMS principal is compromised (rotation playbook + forensic artifacts we would hand over). I'll drop a short draft after lunch.

Sam L: Noted. Closing loop: job 3421 logs retained in secure bucket with access limited to security and SRE.

Priya N: Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
